To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized a series of new benzothiazole derivatives, and these compounds have been found to be active antitumour compounds in vitro.
the synthesis of a series new antitumor agents has been reported via the hypovalent iodine mediated oxidative cyclization of 2-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)-2-phenyl-1,3-benzothiazoles.
the synthesis of new antitumor compounds is reported and the compounds were found to be potent antitumor agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antitumor agents.
the design of new antitumor compounds based on the benzothiazoles and their derivatives.
the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel benzothiazole derivatives with antitumour properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antitumour activities of the compounds reported here are not related to the presence of the benzothiazoles, but rather to the 4-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl substituent.
the 2-substituted benzothiazoles are potent antitumour compounds and the antitumour effect is not only due to a single substituent, but is a combination of the substituents in the benzothiazoles.
the 2-phenybenzothiazole substituted 4-quinol ethers and ester are potent antitumour compounds with a high degree of selectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the benzothiazolyl quinol ethers 1a, 3a, 4a, 4c, 5a, and 6a, and the ester derivatives 1b, 3b, 4b, 4c and 4d are potent antitumour compounds with activity against the human colon and breast tumour cell lines HCT-15 and MCF-7, respectively.
the antitumour activities of the quinol ethers are comparable to that of the quinols and the quinol esters are more active than the quinol ether and quinol derivatives.
we have developed a new class of benzothiazoles that are active against cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2-phenyldihydrobenzothiazole core structure is a good scaffold for the development of novel antitumour drugs.
the benzothiazolyl quinol ethers are potent cytotoxic agents with IC50 values of 0.1-2.5 nM against human colon cancer cell line HT29.
the benzothiazolyl group can be incorporated into a quinol structure to yield a new class of antitumour agent.
